skill.name: claude-settings-audit
skill.description: Analyze repository tooling and existing Claude Code settings to recommend permission allowlists, WebFetch domains, and MCP configuration notes.
skill.summary: Audit repository tooling and recommend Claude Code permission settings.
skill.author: getsentry

security_audit.summary: The static Ruby backtick findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and inline command examples. A real semantic issue remains: the skill recommends broad wildcard Claude Code Bash permissions that can allow non-read-only or sensitive actions.

remediation.issue: Wildcard Bash permissions are broader than the stated read-only goal.
remediation.suggestion: Replace Bash(command:*) entries with narrow command patterns that pin safe flags and deny write-capable options.

remediation.issue: GitHub CLI API access is allowed with arbitrary arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Remove Bash(gh api:*) or replace it with specific read-only gh commands and endpoints.

remediation.issue: MCP examples reference API key environment variables.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users to keep token values in their environment and never commit literal secrets to .mcp.json.

semantic_findings.title: Overbroad Claude Code Bash Allowlist
semantic_findings.description: The skill recommends wildcard Bash permissions such as Bash(find:*), Bash(cat:*), and Bash(gh api:*). These wildcards are described as allowing any arguments, which can permit destructive find options, broad file reads, or GitHub API writes.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The allowlist explicitly includes broad wildcard commands and later states that :* allows any arguments. Several listed commands are not guaranteed read-only when arbitrary arguments are permitted.

content.value_statement: Unsafe or missing Claude Code permissions can slow repository setup and create avoidable risk. This skill inspects project tooling and proposes settings that match detected files and services.
actual_capabilities: Detects common language, package manager, build, infrastructure, and monorepo indicator files.
Checks existing .claude/settings.json content when present in the repository.
Recommends Claude Code permission allow entries based on detected project tools.
Suggests WebFetch domains for Sentry, GitHub, and detected frameworks.
Identifies when Sentry or Linear MCP configuration may be useful.
Provides merge guidance when a project already has Claude Code settings.
limitations: It relies on repository files and may miss tools that are only documented elsewhere.
Recommended command patterns need human review before use in sensitive repositories.
It does not prove that every command pattern is safe for all arguments.
It does not install MCP servers or modify settings files by itself.

use_cases.title: Set up a new repository
use_cases.description: Generate initial Claude Code settings from detected project files and package managers.
use_cases.target_user: Developers onboarding Claude Code to an existing codebase

use_cases.title: Review existing permissions
use_cases.description: Compare current settings with detected tooling and identify missing or unnecessary entries.

use_cases.title: Prepare Sentry project tooling
use_cases.description: Find Sentry-specific signals and suggest related skills, documentation domains, and MCP notes.
use_cases.target_user: Sentry maintainers and internal developer experience teams

prompt_templates.title: Basic Repository Audit
prompt_templates.scenario: You want a first permissions recommendation for a project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this repository and recommend Claude Code settings for read-only project inspection.

prompt_templates.title: Existing Settings Review
prompt_templates.scenario: A repository already has Claude Code settings.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the existing .claude/settings.json and explain what should be kept, removed, or added.

prompt_templates.title: Monorepo Permission Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: A repository contains several languages or package managers.
prompt_templates.prompt: Detect each workspace in this monorepo and propose Claude Code permissions for the tools actually present.

prompt_templates.title: Security-Focused Allowlist Review
prompt_templates.scenario: You need strict permissions for a sensitive repository.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the proposed Claude Code allowlist and identify any command patterns that are broader than read-only access.

output_examples.input: A Python service with poetry.lock, Dockerfile, Makefile, and existing Claude Code settings.
output: A summary table listing Python, Poetry, Docker, Make, and any detected services.
A recommended settings section grouped by baseline, Python, Docker, and Make commands.
Merge notes that explain which existing permissions should stay or be narrowed.

output_examples.input: A Node.js monorepo with pnpm-lock.yaml, turbo.json, React, and Sentry packages.
output: A detected stack summary for Node.js, pnpm, Turborepo, React, and Sentry.
A permissions recommendation focused on pnpm and repository inspection commands.
WebFetch and Sentry skill suggestions tied to the detected framework and service.

output_examples.input: A repository with Terraform files and no current Claude Code configuration.
output: A warning to review infrastructure-related commands before adding them.
A first settings recommendation limited to detected infrastructure tooling.
Notes about keeping secrets out of MCP and settings files.

best_practices: Review every recommended wildcard permission before adding it to a shared repository.
Keep literal API tokens out of .mcp.json and use environment variables instead.
Regenerate recommendations after package managers, frameworks, or build tools change.
anti_patterns: Do not approve broad Bash wildcards without checking whether each command can write or delete data.
Do not include commands for package managers that are not used by the repository.
Do not commit generated settings before a human reviews the permission scope.

faq.question: Does this skill change my settings file?
faq.answer: No. It produces recommendations and merge guidance for a human to review.

faq.question: Can it detect every framework in a repository?
faq.answer: No. It checks common files and dependencies, so unusual setups may need manual review.

faq.question: Why does it inspect package manager files?
faq.answer: Those files show which tools are actually used, which helps avoid unnecessary permissions.

faq.question: Should I accept every suggested Bash permission?
faq.answer: No. Review wildcard permissions carefully because some commands can write data with certain arguments.

faq.question: Does it support Sentry projects?
faq.answer: Yes. It looks for Sentry dependencies and suggests related domains, skills, and MCP configuration notes.

faq.question: Can Codex use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
